significance_rule.method: Bonferroni correction across the 5 paired tier comparisons
significance_rule.note: A tier comparison is marked significant only if its permutation p-value -- computed with the same metric as its reported confidence interval (tie-aware AUPRC for auprc_diffs) -- clears the Bonferroni-corrected per-comparison alpha (0.01) AND its paired bootstrap 95% CI excludes zero. The `significant` flags on auprc_diffs use variant-level inference only; a tier claim ALSO needs its gene-clustered 95% CI to exclude zero (see gene_clustered_cis). M2-M1: WITHDRAW 'M2 best tier' as a claim: gene-clustered 95% CI for the M2-M1 tie-aware AUPRC gain includes zero; report as a non-significant descriptive difference.

correction_note: 2026-11-09 no-CADD refit supersedes the pre-rebuild record. Pre-rebuild: the feature matrix had cadd_phred = -1.0 for all 60,521 rows, so M1 never saw a real CADD value; M4-M1 +0.0509 (significant:true) was the headline of that run and is DEAD -- it survives only under auprc_diffs_superseded_pre_rebuild. Rebuilt-matrix run (2026-11-08) still had the defect in a subtler form: real CADD values in validation/test, but the fitted coefficient was fit on a constant in train (0/35,921 scored), so test-time CADD signal entered through an uncalibrated coefficient; its tie-corrected values (M4-M1 -0.0069) are preserved under tie_corrected_superseded_pre_refit. Live values are the *_refit_no_cadd sections. The M2-M1 (+0.0310) and M3-M1 (+0.0317) step-AUPRC gains in the pre-rebuild run were a tie-breaking artifact: a 6,077-variant tie block (test SNVs with am_missing=1 and review_stars=1) penalised M1 step AUPRC by -0.0318; tie-corrected gains on the pre-rebuild matrix were M2-M1 +0.0006 and M3-M1 -0.0002.
